night.text: On April 26, 1986, a safety test at reactor four went wrong, and the reactor exploded.

toll.text: 31 people died in the immediate aftermath. Pripyat's 49,000 people were evacuated, and about 350,000 were relocated in all.

pripyat.text: But imagine the test went fine. Pripyat could still be a living city, and the exclusion zone could be farmland.

nuclear.text: Chernobyl made the world fear nuclear power. Italy voted to quit it in 1987. Without that fear, more reactors might have been built, and less coal burned.

soviet.text: Gorbachev wrote that Chernobyl was perhaps the real cause of the Soviet collapse. Without it, the USSR might have lasted longer.

wildlife.text: The twist? Wolves, lynx and Przewalski's horses now thrive in the empty zone. That refuge wouldn't exist. So, would the world be better? Comment below.
